lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Ten customers in fiscal years 2025 and 2024 and nine customers in fiscal year 2023 accounted for approximately 93 %, 92 %, and 92 % of the Company’s net sales and revenue, respectively.
Our ethanol plants rely upon third parties for their supply of natural gas, which is consumed as fuel in the production process.
We depend on our partners to operate certain of our ethanol investments .
The growth of our ethanol business depends on our ability to identify and develop new ethanol investments.
Any expansion strategy will depend on prevailing market conditions for the price of ethanol and the cost of corn and natural gas and the expectations of future market conditions.
Flexible fuel vehicles (“FFVs”) receive preferential treatment in meeting federally mandated corporate average fuel economy (“CAFE”) standards for automobiles manufactured by car makers.
Our revenue from the sale of distillers grains depends upon its continued market acceptance as an animal feed.
Our plants depend on an uninterrupted supply of energy and water to operate.
We generally rely on third parties to provide these resources.

We rely on information technology in our operations and financial reporting and any material failure, inadequacy, interruption or security breach of that technology could harm our ability to efficiently operate our business and report our financial results accurately and timely.
Our primary sources of cash have been income from operations.

x.name: Big River
f: Retained Earnings, Undistributed Earnings from Equity Method Investees
Retained Earnings, Undistributed Earnings from Equity Method Investees

s.t: During the second quarter of fiscal year 2026, we recognized income from our equity investment in Big River of approximately $7.2 million compared to income of approximately $0.9 million for the second quarter of fiscal year 2025.

During the first six months of fiscal year 2026, we recognized income from our equity investment in Big River of approximately $10.8 million compared to income of approximately $1.9 million for the first six months of fiscal year 2025.
The Company accounts for its investment in Big River using the equity method of accounting and includes the results on a delayed basis of one month as Big River has a fiscal year end of December 31.

The Company includes the results of operations of One Earth and the equity investment income of Big River in its Consolidated Statements of Operations on a delayed basis of one month as One Earth and Big River have fiscal year ends of December 31.

Our investment in Big River, which has interests in four ethanol production plants, represents an effective ownership of approximately 40.8 million gallons of ethanol shipped in the trailing twelve months ended July 31, 2026.

x.name: Big River
f: Payments to Acquire Equity Method Investments
Equity Method Investment, Underlying Equity in Net Assets

s.t: At January 31, 2026, the carrying value of the investment in Big River was approximately $ 37.8 million; the amount of underlying equity in the net assets of Big River was approximately $ 41.0 million.
We are currently invested in three ethanol production entities – One Earth Energy, LLC, NuGen Energy, LLC, and Big River Resources, LLC. We own a majority interest in One Earth and NuGen.

Equity in Income of Unconsolidated Ethanol Affiliates – During fiscal years 2025 and 2024, we recognized income of approximately $12.5 million and $9.4 million, respectively, from our equity investment in Big River Resources, LLC (“Big River”).

Our investment in Big River, which has interests in four ethanol production plants, represents an effective ownership of approximately 38.6 million gallons of ethanol shipped in the trailing twelve months ended January 31, 2026.

We expect the operating experience of Big River to be generally consistent with the trends in crush spread margins described in the “Overview” section as Big River’s results are dependent on the same industry dynamics as our other ethanol investments (ethanol, corn, dried distillers grains and natural gas pricing).
Approximately 2.4% of our net assets are restricted pursuant to the terms of various loan agreements of Big River, our equity method investee, as of January 31, 2026.

The Company accounts for its investment in Big River using the equity method of accounting and includes the results of Big River on a delayed basis of one month as it has a fiscal year end of December 31.
The Company’s equity method investment in Big River Resources, LLC (“Big River”) is accounted for under ASC 323.
